chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of the students known as Ra's al-Madary, who said:
I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The best place for the two feet for the prayer is the two slippers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the best place for the feet during prayer according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies the 'two slippers' (al-na'lan) as the most preferable place for the feet during prayer, a ruling that highlights the virtue of maintaining ritual purity (taharah) through clean footwear. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it supports the permissibility and preference of praying with shoes, provided they are clean, contrasting with practices that strictly require bare feet on specific prayer mats. The emphasis on 'slippers' rather than just 'shoes' may also reflect the specific footwear of the era, underscoring the general principle of cleanliness and modesty in the posture of worship.
